channel.title: PanPan Marine Blog
channel.description: Underwater robotics buying guides and procurement planning.

item.title: Fish Farm Net and Mooring Inspection with Small ROVs
item.description: Plan net-pen and mooring inspection with small ROVs: what to inspect, how to avoid entanglement, biosecurity, cold water and how to choose between compact inspection vehicles.

item.title: How Much Floating Debris Can a Cleaning Vessel Collect in a Day?
item.description: Estimate the daily collection of an autonomous cleaning vessel from basket size, unloading trips, operating hours and debris density, and why rated coverage differs from real results.

item.title: Autonomous Surface Cleaning Vessels for Harbours and Reservoirs: A Buyer’s Guide
item.description: How to choose an autonomous trash-skimming vessel: debris volume, water area, vessel size, docking and charging, local approvals and how to verify cleaning results.

item.title: Underwater Trash Rack Cleaning: Robotic Options, Risks and Acceptance Tests
item.description: How robotic trash-rack cleaning works, when it suits a hydropower intake, what to survey first and how to agree acceptance tests, with a crawler cleaning robot example.

item.title: Launch and Recovery for a 200–500 kg ROV: Crane, A-Frame or Davit?
item.description: Compare cranes, A-frames and davits for launching and recovering light work-class and work-class ROVs, and plan deck space, crew, sea state and when a TMS is needed.

item.title: Subsea Cable Route and Burial-Depth Surveys: Sensors, ROV Class and Deliverables
item.description: Plan subsea cable inspection: visual surveys, seabed mapping, burial-depth measurement and free-span checks, with the sensors, ROV class, positioning and reports each needs.

item.title: Observation-Class vs Work-Class ROV: The Practical Difference
item.description: Compare observation-class and work-class ROVs by weight, payload, thrust, deployment, crew and cost of operation, with examples from 42 kg to 520 kg.

item.title: Offshore Wind Monopile and Scour Inspection with ROVs: What to Specify
item.description: Plan ROV inspection of offshore wind monopiles and scour protection: the deliverables owners expect, the sensors each needs, ROV class, weather windows and data.

item.title: Dam Inspection: When to Use a Swimming ROV and When to Use a Crawler
item.description: Compare free-swimming ROVs and crawler robots for dam, intake and gate inspection: flow, surface condition, coverage, data and deployment. Includes a decision table.

item.title: How Long Should an ROV Tether Be?
item.description: Estimate ROV tether length from depth, horizontal distance, route and slack, and understand the trade-offs: drag, power, handling and buoyancy.

item.title: Penstock and Headrace Tunnel Inspection Without Dewatering: A Planning Guide
item.description: When can a flooded penstock or headrace tunnel be inspected without draining it? Compare wet and dry inspection, then plan flow, access, tether, positioning, recovery and deliverables.

item.title: What an ROV Depth Rating Does — and Doesn’t — Tell You
item.description: An ROV depth rating describes the vehicle’s pressure housings, not the whole system. Learn what else limits working depth and how to specify depth correctly.

item.title: How Much Payload Does an Inspection ROV Really Need?
item.description: Work out the payload an inspection ROV must carry: in-water weight, trim, tether drag and the sensors your inspection result needs. Includes a worksheet and R-30/R-45 example.

item.title: Underwater Cleaning vs Dredging: Choosing the Right System
item.description: Compare underwater surface cleaning and sediment removal. Define deposits, access, pumps, separation and acceptance before choosing an A-80 or AD-100 system.

item.title: How to Choose an Industrial Inspection ROV
item.description: Choose an industrial inspection ROV around visibility, access, payload, useful data and complete system cost. Includes an R-30/R-45 comparison and buyer checklist.

item.title: Flooded Tunnel Inspection: A Procurement Planning Guide
item.description: Plan flooded tunnel inspection procurement: engineering inputs, tether and sensor scope, AD-400 range evidence, acceptance data and complete-system costs.
